finding: The live range of $1,150-$4,800 is about right at both ends; it is wide because the turbocharger itself runs from about $500 to over $3,400 depending on the vehicle and on whether an aftermarket or genuine unit is used. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks), for the turbocharger alone: economy 2014 Cruze 1.4L about $835-$1,174 (2.4 hr); midsize 2017 CR-V 1.5L about $1,011-$3,295 (2.8-6.3 hr); truck 2015 F-150 3.5L EcoBoost, one turbo, about $975-$1,711 (4.0 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $1,802-$4,307 (5.5 hr). The lowest builds (about $835-$975) sit below the live $1,150, but they pair an aftermarket unit at an online price with a short labor time and leave out the oil lines, gaskets, oil change and coolant that a proper job includes; with those added, $1,150 is a fair floor, and the lowest benchmark is $1,500. The $4,800 top fits: a genuine BMW exchange unit at list ($3,427) plus 5.5 hours is about $4,307 before lines and fluids, and RepairPal's top figure for the 328i is $4,674. Replacing both turbochargers on the F-150 is a bigger job: Ford allows 4.9 hours for diagnosing and replacing the pair, and two genuine units list at about $2,060, so roughly $2,650-$2,850 at list before extras. Second look on 2026-11-20: a further search of manufacturer bulletins (Honda and Acura 1.5L/2.0L turbo, GM 1.5L Malibu and 2.7L/3.0L Silverado, Ford 2.0L/2.7L/3.5L EcoBoost, Hyundai and Kia 2.0L turbo, Mazda 2.5L turbo) and of BMW parts sellers found no turbocharger-replacement time for the CR-V, the 328i, or any common midsize or luxury vehicle that could replace them as the example, so no example was changed and no parts figure was changed. Two hour figures were tightened to keep diagnosis out of the range: the Cruze high was 2.7 hr (2.4 hr plus GM's 0.3 hr boost test) and is now 2.4 hr; the F-150 low was Ford's 2.8 hr, which is a 'diagnose and replace' time, and is now a cross-check only. How solid the labor times are: the Cruze figure is GM's own warranty time for replacing the turbocharger on that car (2.4 hr), and is the only hour figure that is both for the example vehicle and for the replacement alone. The F-150 now rests on a single figure, a parts seller's 'approx 4 hours' for earlier model years (2011-2012); Ford's own diagnose-and-replace times for the 2015 truck (2.8 hr left, 3.4 hr right) are lower even with diagnosis included, so 4 hours is a shop-side figure rather than a warranty one. The CR-V and the BMW have no stated time for the vehicle itself. The CR-V range borrows GM's 2.8 hr for a smaller crossover and a named mechanic's 6.3 hr example for a 2017 Malibu 1.5L turbo; the BMW uses a single figure, the same mechanic's 5.5 hr example for a 2017 Audi A4 2.0L turbo, and that article does not say where its times come from. Treat the midsize, truck and luxury labor as rough. Confidence stays low: only two of the eight hour figures are for the example vehicle, and the truck and luxury classes each rest on one figure. Our mainstream totals sit below RepairPal's national figure ($2,631-$3,261) mostly on parts: its parts figure is $1,874-$2,151, while genuine list prices we can cite are $790 (Cruze) and $990-$1,071 (F-150 each side); the CR-V ($2,287) and BMW ($3,427) genuine units are in or above that range.
extras: A quote usually adds new oil feed and return lines and gaskets (many makers call for new lines so the new turbocharger is not starved of oil), an engine oil and filter change, coolant, a diagnosis or boost-system test, shop supplies and sales tax. One named mechanic's worked example for a 2017 Malibu lists lines $163, gasket $33, coolant $50 and an oil change $89 on top of the turbocharger. Genuine exchange units carry a refundable core charge ($350 on the Honda and $590 on the BMW listings seen). If the old unit failed and shed oil or metal, the intercooler and intake piping must be cleaned or replaced, and the cause of the failure (oil supply, air leaks, a clogged air filter or outlet pipe) has to be fixed or the new one can fail too. On twin-turbo engines the second turbocharger is a separate cost.
